concepts.name: HTML elements and attributes
concepts.summary: Recognise that HTML marks up content with opening and closing tags, nested elements and attributes such as href, src and alt.

concepts.name: Document skeleton structure
concepts.summary: Explain the roles of the doctype, html, head and body and what belongs in each.

concepts.name: Text content elements
concepts.summary: Choose headings, paragraphs, lists, links and images to mark up basic content correctly.

concepts.name: CSS rule syntax
concepts.summary: Read and explain a rule made of a selector and declarations of property and value pairs.

concepts.name: Linking CSS to HTML
concepts.summary: Name the three ways to apply CSS and recognise the link element for external stylesheets.

concepts.name: Basic selectors
concepts.summary: Understand how element, class and id selectors pick which elements a rule applies to.

concepts.name: Common text and color properties
concepts.summary: Recall properties that change color, font, size and background of elements.

misconceptions.text: HTML is used to control the visual design of a page, such as colors and layout.
Headings should be chosen by how big they look rather than by their meaning.
Content in the head element is displayed on the page.

concepts.name: Semantic page elements
concepts.summary: Apply header, nav, main, section, article, aside and footer to give a page meaningful structure.

concepts.name: Box model
concepts.summary: Use content, padding, border and margin to size and space elements and predict their rendered size.

concepts.name: Block and inline display
concepts.summary: Explain how block, inline and inline-block elements flow and which properties apply to each.

concepts.name: Forms and inputs
concepts.summary: Build a form with labelled inputs, buttons and appropriate input types.

concepts.name: Cascade and specificity
concepts.summary: Predict which declaration wins using source order, specificity and inheritance.

concepts.name: Combinators and pseudo-classes
concepts.summary: Write selectors using descendant and child combinators and states like :hover and :focus.

concepts.name: CSS units and values
concepts.summary: Distinguish absolute and relative units and choose among them for sizes and colors.

concepts.name: Accessible images and links
concepts.summary: Write useful alt text and descriptive link text for images and links.

misconceptions.text: The width property sets the total visible width of an element including padding and border.
An id selector and class selector have the same weight, so the last rule always wins.
Semantic elements like section and nav look different by default, so they are only for styling.

concepts.name: Flexbox layout
concepts.summary: Lay out items in a row or column using flex direction, alignment, wrapping and gap.

concepts.name: Flex item sizing
concepts.summary: Analyse how grow, shrink and basis distribute free space among flex items.

concepts.name: CSS Grid layout
concepts.summary: Define two-dimensional layouts with grid tracks, fr units, gaps and item placement.

concepts.name: Positioning and stacking
concepts.summary: Analyse how position values, containing blocks and stacking order place elements.

concepts.name: Media queries
concepts.summary: Adapt styles to viewport conditions with media queries and the viewport meta tag.

concepts.name: Mobile-first responsive approach
concepts.summary: Structure CSS from a small-screen base with fluid widths and flexible images, adding enhancements at larger sizes.

concepts.name: Margin collapsing and normal flow
concepts.summary: Diagnose spacing problems caused by margin collapse and normal flow behavior.

concepts.name: Choosing flex or grid
concepts.summary: Compare flexbox and grid and select the right one for a given layout problem.

misconceptions.text: Flexbox and grid are interchangeable and grid is simply a newer replacement for flexbox.
Position absolute places an element relative to the page regardless of its ancestors.
Responsive design means building a separate mobile site with media queries only.

concepts.name: Custom properties and theming
concepts.summary: Use custom properties with inheritance to build maintainable themes and design tokens.

concepts.name: Fluid sizing functions
concepts.summary: Use clamp, min, max and viewport units to create fluid type and spacing with fewer breakpoints.

concepts.name: Advanced grid patterns
concepts.summary: Build intrinsically responsive grids with auto-fit, minmax and named areas.

concepts.name: CSS architecture and naming
concepts.summary: Evaluate methods for organising CSS so specificity stays low and styles remain scalable.

concepts.name: Accessible markup and ARIA
concepts.summary: Evaluate pages for keyboard access, contrast, landmarks and appropriate use of ARIA.

concepts.name: Transitions and animations
concepts.summary: Apply transitions and keyframe animations of cheap properties while respecting reduced motion preferences.

concepts.name: Responsive images and media
concepts.summary: Serve appropriate image sources with srcset, sizes and picture, avoiding layout shift.

concepts.name: Container and modern selectors
concepts.summary: Judge when container queries and selectors like :has or :where give better component-level styling than viewport queries.

misconceptions.text: ARIA attributes should be added everywhere to make a page accessible.
Animating any property is equally cheap for browser performance.
Using more specific selectors and !important is the right way to manage overrides in large stylesheets.

concepts.name: Rendering pipeline and performance
concepts.summary: Evaluate how CSS and HTML choices affect parsing, layout, paint and compositing and so page speed.

concepts.name: Intrinsic and algorithmic layout
concepts.summary: Create layouts that adapt from content and available space through min-content, max-content and flexible primitives.

concepts.name: Internationalisation and logical properties
concepts.summary: Evaluate and build layouts that work across writing directions using logical properties.

concepts.name: Cross-browser and progressive enhancement
concepts.summary: Judge support trade-offs and design fallbacks using feature queries and progressive enhancement.

concepts.name: Accessibility auditing strategy
concepts.summary: Plan and evaluate audits combining automated checks, keyboard and screen reader testing against standards.

concepts.name: Advanced CSS engineering patterns
concepts.summary: Create robust cascade strategies using layers, scoping and low-specificity conventions for large codebases.

concepts.name: Design system architecture
concepts.summary: Design a scalable CSS system of tokens, layers and component patterns shared across projects.

misconceptions.text: Minified or fewer CSS rules alone determine page performance, regardless of render-blocking and layout cost.
Passing an automated accessibility checker means a page is accessible.
Physical properties like left and margin-left are sufficient for any international site.
